newsitem.title: JAPAN: June JGB put options cast pall over market-traders.
newsitem.headline: June JGB put options cast pall over market-traders.

text.p: The sharp fall in the key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures on Tuesday morning may have been triggered by sales from hedge funds, which are said to be holding a large amount of June JGB futures put options with a strike price of 123.00, traders said on Tuesday.
Large-lot selling of the June JGB futures contract in the early morning triggered a fall in the JGB market, traders said.
"A large-lot offer worth 700 contracts was seen this morning around 123.45 and this triggered the fall in JGBs. An additional 300 contracts were sold later on," a senior city bank trader said.

Traders said there was widespread speculation that hedge funds, rumoured to be holders of a large volume of June JGB futures put options at 123.00, were selling June JGB futures this morning in an attempt to bring those put options into the money before they expire at the end of this week.
The key June 10-year JGB futures contract stood at 123.10 by midday, down sharply from the previous day's close of 123.66.
Open interest in the 123.00 June JGB futures put options totalled 12,564 contracts as of Monday's close.
About half of that open interest may be due to long positions held by hedge funds, said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
"It is almost certain that hedge funds are holding them (the 123.00 put options). They probably first bought the options in...April," he said.
He added that open interest on the 123.00 June JGB puts increased by one trillion yen (10,000 contracts) in a single week in April.
Another city bank trader said: "Around April 15 and April 16, open interest increased by several thousand contracts per day."
Active buying by hedge funds at this time, when the premium on the 123.00 June JGB puts was around 0.07, was probably largely responsible for the sharp increase in open interest, traders said.
The premium on the puts has since risen sharply, trading at 0.39 at midday on Tuesday, up from the previous day's close of 0.25. Turnover was 1,454 contracts.

In April, June JGB futures set an all-time high for any benchmark futures contract of 127.34, and many traders were puzzled by the heavy buying of the 123.00 put options at the time, which were far out-of-the-money.
Hedge funds which bought the puts at a premium of 0.07 will probably hold them until expiry, an options trader for a foreign brokerage house said.

"All they have to lose is 0.07 yen, which is like dirt for them. Besides, they probably have already reaped profits by selling above 124.00 the JGB futures they had bought earlier for hedging (against their put options)," he said.

The tumble in June JGBs this morning was exacerbated by selling of futures by option dealers who were delta hedging short positions in the 123.00 June JGB puts, a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
The option dealers are hedging against a further fall in June JGBs below the put options' strike price of 123.00.
